document_title: 829 Acres, 20 Years, and a Notice That Named No Tenant
post_copy:
On January 30th the University of Alaska put 829 acres at Port MacKenzie up for lease on a notice that named no tenant.
Terra Energy signed a 20-year lease in late May for a campus the lease calls "a large-scale industrial park," UA's land director Adrienne Stolpe told the Mat-Su Sentinel.

The Mat-Su Assembly overrode a veto 6-1 in March to market borough land jointly with Terra to big power users like data centers. Yet the university signed without telling borough officials. To port manager Dave Griffin, that "blows my mind."

Per the Mat-Su Sentinel, major state land actions need a best interest finding that weighs public comment, and university land is exempt.

Four parcels to scale and the notice's dates, the rent by year, the affiliate's coal plan and the 6-1 vote.

Should a 20-year university lease stay exempt from the best interest finding?

#PortMacKenzie #LandUse #UALand

slides.kicker: UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA LAND · PORT MACKENZIE
slides.headline: 829 acres. 20 years.
Terra Energy is the tenant.
slides.body: Signed in late May for 20 years. The lease describes the Terra Energy Center Campus as "a large-scale industrial park," with energy generation, transmission, storage and distribution among its uses, and lets Terra sublease to future tenants.

slides.headline: An inholding in the borough's port.
slides.body: The four parcels sit inside the Mat-Su Borough's 8,000-acre port district. Borough officials weren't told before the university signed. Port manager Dave Griffin said it "blows my mind."
labels: TERRA'S PLAN CONFIDENTIAL, PER THE UNIVERSITY

slides.headline: Comment was asked on a notice that named no lessee and no use.
slides.body: Posted January 30th. Comments closed at 5 p.m. on March 2nd. The lease was signed in late May, per university officials.

slides.headline: University land skips the best interest finding.
slides.body: Projects on university land are exempt from the finding the state requires for major actions on state land, per the Mat-Su Sentinel.

slides.headline: $20,000 the first year. $586,000 once it operates.
slides.body: Then $60,000 a year in years two and three. Construction would begin in 2029, and the report gives no figure for that year. Operations are targeted for 2030, and rent would rise 2 percent a year to the end of the 20-year lease.

slides.headline: The campus is part of a coal plan.
slides.body: Flatlands Energy plans a coal plant near Skwentna. DOE selected the project for $89 million in engineering funding for a planned 1,250 MW plant and lists data centers among the loads it would serve. The university's own information doesn't highlight data centers.

slides.headline: The borough markets land with Terra.
slides.body: In March the Assembly overrode a veto 6-1 to court large power users with Terra, data centers among them. Officials expect Terra to seek about 1,000 borough acres near the port.

aftercare: Post this draft Thursday October 8th between 8 and 11 a.m. AKT if it fits your cadence. Tuesday to Thursday mornings are the strongest slots, and drafts arrive daily, so when it goes up is your call.
Paste the sources block as the first comment within 60 seconds of posting. Keep every raw URL as plain text so LinkedIn keeps the links.
Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes, especially anyone from UA, the borough or Terra. Point lease questions back to the Sentinel's report, since the lease itself isn't public.
After 48 hours, note saves, comments and reposts, plus whether replies took up the caption's exemption question or the close slide's notice question.
editor_notes_for_email: The lease isn't public. Its term, signing date and every rent figure come from university officials quoted in the Mat-Su Sentinel on October 6th, and ADN's same-day piece is a republication, not a second source. Terra hadn't responded as of that report, so a statement from Terra or UA after posting may move these numbers. Watch the comments for anyone saying the borough approved 1,000 acres or that the UA lease is for a data center, because neither is in the record.
